newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's insurance turnover up to $794.6 mln/95.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's insurance turnover up to $794.6 mln/95.

text.p: Morocco's insurance turnover rose 8.75 percent to 6.8 billion dirhams ($794.6 million) in 1995 compared with the previous year, due mainly to the expansion of car insurance sector, the authoritative Centre Marocain de Conjoncture (CMC) said.

"Insurance companies activity registered a sustained increase to reach 6.83 billion dirhams turnover in 1995, up from 6.28 billion dirhams in 1994," the CMC think-tank said in a report received on Tuesday.
Among the country's 21 insurance firms, a group of six companies held nearly 60 percent of market share or 4.04 billion dirhams turnover in 1995, the Casablanca-based CMC said.
The group is Compagnie d'Assurance des Transports, Wataniya, Al-Amane, Compagnie Africaine d'Assurances, Compagnie Nord Africaine et Internationale d'Assurances and WAFA Assurances.
The centre said car insurance was the most active compared with other sectors like fire, maritime and aviation insurance.
"As result of its expansion, car insurance net premium rose to 2.7 billion dirhams in 1995 from 2.3 billion dirhams in the previous year," it said.
But aviation, fire and maritime insurance premium pursued a negative trend registering a decline of between minus 8.9 percent and minus 0.34 percent last year, the report said.
The range of insurance products offered to different clients has to be improved in order to boost the sector, it said.

"Insurance sector remains underdeveloped compared with other emerging markets. Morocco spends an average $30 per head a year for insurance compared with the neighbouring North African Tunisia which devotes $38 per head annually," Anas Alami, analyst at Upline Securities said.
The government is pushing for restructuring and modernisation of the whole sector to meet the World Bank urgent demands, he said.
In October 1995, the authorities announced officially the dissolution "for mismanagement" of ARABIA, CADA, REMAR, RENAISSANCE and VICTOIRE insurance companies.
The liquidation of the six firms left a total deficit of an estimated 6.0 billion dirhams, Upline Securities said.
Insurance sector represented an average 3.0 percent of Morocco's Gross domestic product in 1995, analysts said.
